turns.query: What is Section 3(p) of the Patents Act?
turns.answer: Section 3(p) of the Patents Act, 1970 states that an invention which, in effect, is traditional knowledge or an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known components is not patentable. Section 3(p) of the Patents Act, 1970 excludes the patenting of traditional knowledge or anything that is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known components.
